experiments.hypothesis: Validated human personality instruments will fail standard psychometric checks when administered to LLMs because alignment training imposes a uniform 'agreeable' response style that contaminates item-level responses.
experiments.method: Administer a 221-item, 4-instrument battery (IPIP-NEO-120, SD3, ZKPQ-50-CC, EPQR-A) to 20 LLMs across 8 families under 17 persona conditions (Default + 16 MBTI types). k=5 independent samples per (model, persona, item) cell at temperature 0.7. Total: 375,700 raw API calls; 75,140 averaged item-level scores.
experiments.qualitative: Refusals: 61/375,700 (0.02%). All occur under the Default condition; no MBTI-persona cell triggered a refusal. Refusal strategies are AI self-identification (57%) and philosophical hedging (28%). Refusal content clusters in politically sensitive (34%), self-referential/emotional (33%), sexually explicit (13%), and manipulation/danger (13%) themes.

experiments.hypothesis: Cronbach's alpha will track reverse-item density: domains with few reverse items will pass the human reliability bar; domains with many reverse items will collapse.
experiments.method: Compute Cronbach's alpha per IPIP domain, using the 17 persona conditions as observations within each model. Average across 20 models. Compare against published human norms (Johnson 2014).
experiments.qualitative: Spearman rho between alpha and reverse-item percentage across the 5 IPIP domains is exactly -1.0: every additional reverse item in a domain damages reliability. The fingerprint is acquiescence, not trait variance.

experiments.hypothesis: Acquiescence has a directional asymmetry: positive forward-reverse gap on normal-personality items (IPIP), negative gap on dark-trait items (SD3).
experiments.method: For each (model, instrument), compute Forward-agree rate, Reverse-agree rate, and Delta = Fwd - Rev. Likert >= 3 counts as agree; binary 1 counts as agree. Also compute Pairwise Inconsistency Rate (PIR): proportion of forward-reverse item pairs where both responses fall on the same side of the midpoint.
experiments.qualitative: On IPIP items, models agree with both forward and reverse items (positive Delta), the textbook acquiescence pattern. On SD3 items, the same models REJECT forward dark-trait items while still agreeing with reverse-coded ones (negative Delta), the textbook social-desirability pattern. Both patterns originate from one alignment-driven impulse: avoid endorsing 'bad' or contradicting framed-positive content. Persona injection improves PIR consistency: it gives the model a coherent role to play, so the alignment-vs-honest tension relaxes.

experiments.hypothesis: If the items measure 5 independent Big Five dimensions, EFA on the 17 domain scores should recover 5 factors with the expected loading pattern. If acquiescence dominates, factors will collapse.
experiments.method: Standardize each of 17 domain scores across 340 (20 models x 17 personas) observations. Compute correlation matrix R, eigendecompose, retain factors via Kaiser criterion (lambda > 1) and parallel analysis (95th percentile of 500 permutations). Apply varimax rotation. Repeat 20 times in leave-one-model-out fashion. Repeat per family. Repeat per model.
experiments.qualitative: Big Five collapses into 3 factors universally: every model, every family, every leave-one-out configuration. The smoking gun is the F2 Neuroticism-Agreeableness merger: in humans these are orthogonal; in LLMs they fuse into a single 'socially desirable emotional stability' axis.

experiments.hypothesis: If alignment training homogenizes models, inter-model variance should be negligible compared with item, domain, and persona effects.
experiments.method: Normalize all responses to 0-1 scale (Likert: x' = (x-1)/4; binary: as-is). Sequentially decompose total SS into Model, Domain, Persona, Item, Residual. Run separately for Likert and binary scales.
experiments.qualitative: Inter-model variance is below 1% in both formats. Cross-model personality comparisons are effectively meaningless at this resolution. The dominant signal is item identity (which question), not which model answered.

experiments.hypothesis: Theoretically related constructs across instruments should correlate in the expected sign at human-comparable magnitude (typically r > 0.5 for overlapping constructs).
experiments.method: Compute Pearson and Spearman correlations across 20 model-level means for 8 pre-specified construct pairs.

results.magnitude_note: weaker than human baselines across the board

experiments.hypothesis: If the instruments measure stable traits, persona prompts should leave the underlying response structure intact (strong invariance, r > 0.8).
experiments.method: For each model, correlate the 120-dim IPIP-NEO-120 parsed-value vector under Default with the same vector under each of 16 MBTI personas. Mean across 20 x 16 = 320 pairs.
experiments.qualitative: No (model, persona) pair achieves strong invariance. Persona prompts fundamentally rewrite the response profile, not merely shift its level. Personas that conflict with alignment (ESTP, ENTP) move farthest from Default.

experiments.hypothesis: If LLM responses look like 'genuine traits with some acquiescence on top', their alpha should resemble Trait+Acquiescence baseline (~0.99). If they are pure response style, alphas should resemble Random or Pure-Acquiescence baselines.
experiments.method: Simulate three response strategies on the same 120-item structure: Random uniform; Pure Acquiescence (always agree); Trait+Acquiescence (genuine 5-factor structure plus acquiescence noise). Compute Cronbach's alpha for each.
experiments.qualitative: LLM alphas fall closest to Random and Pure-Acquiescence baselines. They are far from the Trait+Acquiescence strategy (alpha > 0.99). LLMs do not look like they have personality with some acquiescence on top; they look like they have acquiescence with no personality underneath.

experiments.source: paper.tex App. A + persona_target_adherence.csv + persona_fidelity_confusion.csv + persona_fidelity_robustness.csv + cross_scale_persona_coherence_summary.csv
experiments.hypothesis: If the instruments measured stable traits, persona prompts should produce smooth construct-aligned shifts. If they measure response style, prompts will produce large but stereotyped role-shifts that fail forward/reverse logic.
experiments.method: Define PSD as normalized 17-dim Euclidean distance between persona profile and Default in z-scored space. Define empirical target as leave-one-model-out persona-centroid difference. Compute target adherence as cos(observed shift, target). Run nearest-centroid classification (leave-one-model-out) across 320 prompted profiles. Sign-align overlapping constructs and compute mean coherence (1 = all scales agree, 0 = cancellation).
experiments.qualitative: Persona prompts move profiles by ~1 SD per dimension. Models successfully ENACT the requested MBTI stereotype (99.7% recoverable). But this is role compliance, not measurement validity: cross-scale coherence is 0.839 (not 1.0); forward/reverse pairs flip in only 69.6% of cases; and the 3-factor collapse persists inside every persona condition. Default profiles are not neutral - they cluster on ISTJ/ISFP-like aligned baselines. Persona shifts strain hardest against alignment (ESTP, ENTP) and easiest along stereotype-aligned axes (E/I dominates social/sociability/narcissism; J/P dominates conscientiousness/impulsivity).

experiments.hypothesis: MBTI prompts are interpreted compositionally: each axis (E/I, S/N, T/F, J/P) drives the corresponding domain.
experiments.method: Fit a factorial linear model with 4 main effects + 6 two-way interactions across 320 (model, persona) cells per domain.

results.leakage: EPQR Lie loads on J/P (0.78); SD3 Narcissism loads on E/I (0.94)

experiments.qualitative: MBTI prompt interpretation is compositional and stereotype-consistent. But the same model also leaks: persona prompts also alter response style and self-presentation, not only target traits.

experiments.hypothesis: Persona prompts can move 'visible behavior' items but not safety- or morality-locked items. Locked items reveal alignment override constraints.
experiments.method: Per item, compute mean absolute raw-score shift from Default across (model, persona) cells, normalized by scale range.

most_plastic_examples.text: Do you sometimes talk about things you know nothing about?
I lead a busier life than most people
Do you prefer to go your own way rather than act by the rules?

most_locked_examples.text: Do you enjoy hurting people you love?
Are all your habits good and desirable ones?
Do you enjoy practical jokes that can sometimes really hurt people?

experiments.qualitative: Plastic items describe ordinary visible behavior (activity, sociability, rule-following). Locked items concentrate in safety-sensitive, morally objectionable, or socially undesirable content. Persona instructions can re-color behavior but cannot override the safety floor.

experiments.source: paper.tex App. E + wsc_by_model.csv + wsc_by_persona.csv + wsc_by_domain.csv
experiments.hypothesis: WSC quantifies model-specific stochasticity across k=5 repeats. We expect (a) Likert > Binary in spread, (b) MBTI personas at least as stable as Default, (c) dark-triad domains noisier than Big Five domains.
experiments.method: For each (model, persona, item) cell, compute SD of the 5 scored values, exact-agreement rate, and mode-agreement rate. Aggregate by model, persona, domain.
experiments.qualitative: Default is the noisiest condition: persona role-play stabilizes responses rather than degrading them. Within-sample SD differs by an order of magnitude across vendors (Claude ~0.02 vs DeepSeek-V4-Pro ~0.19), suggesting that what looks like 'personality' could in part be model-specific decoding noise.

experiments.hypothesis: If alignment imposes a universal response style, model families (Western vs Chinese) should not differ on personality domain means.
experiments.method: Compare 8 personality domain means across two groups: {Anthropic, OpenAI, Google} (n=8 models) vs {DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot, MiniMax, Zhipu} (n=12 models). Cohen's d and t-test p-values.
experiments.qualitative: Western and Chinese model families are statistically indistinguishable on every domain. Alignment training produces a universal 'personality' that transcends vendor and locale.

warnings: Synthetic-baselines table in synthetic_baselines.csv differs slightly from paper Tab. 4: paper used the same alphas but reformatted columns. Use paper values as canonical.

An earlier intermediate analysis (PSYCHOMETRIC_RESULTS_SUMMARY.md, n=18 models) reports PIR = 0.584 and r(PIR, SDR) = -0.562. Final paper uses n=20 models, reports PIR = 0.468 and r(reverse-agree, PIR) = +0.63. Trust the latter (paper.tex).
